fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Cloud and Jira DC currently nest retries across subprocess, SDK, wrapper, and reconciler layers. A non-idempotent ticket write can therefore exceed a predictable request budget or be replayed after an ambiguous commit. This task defines the provider-neutral logical-operation contract before either adapter changes.

## Approach
Create immutable operation/outcome values plus one fake-clock retry-budget owner in the reconciler domain. Adapter layers report one physical invocation at a time; they do not sleep or replay. This keeps the approved retry envelope in one place while preserving the additive-jitter behavior already accepted in ADR 0084.

The contract is exact:
- `logical_id` is one canonical UUID string generated once per logical operation, retained across every invocation or observation.
- `Disposition` has exactly `applied`, `already_satisfied`, `recovered`, `retryable_deferred`, `commit_unknown`, `permanent_failure`, `exhausted_transient`, `dependency_deferred`, `scope_deferred`, `safety_aborted`, `skipped`.
- `FailureScope` has exactly `none`, `ticket`, `endpoint`, `tenant`, `provider`, `global`.
- `ReplaySafety` has exactly `not_applicable`, `safe`, `observe_first`, `forbidden`.
- `DelaySource` has exactly `none`, `fallback_jitter`, `provider`, `fuse`.
- Enum values serialize as the lowercase strings above. Invocation/request totals are non-negative integers. Durations serialize as integer milliseconds. `retry_not_before` is UTC RFC 3339 with `Z`.
- Canonical bytes route through `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` with its default `ascii_only=False`; no inline JSON serializer is added. Equivalent outcomes therefore produce byte-identical sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON.
- `invocation_count` is the number already executed, ranging from 0 through 3. `retry_index` is zero-based: index 0 selects `[2s,3s)` while index 1 selects `[4s,5s)` using `2**(retry_index+1)+U[0,1)`.
- Diagnostic entries are chronological immutable mappings. Only `stage`, `category`, `status_code`, `provider_code`, `retry_after_ms`, `message` are admitted; optional absent keys are omitted. Raw headers, request/response bodies, credentials, ticket content are never admitted. Message redaction calls the public `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` seam with only the `message` key, then applies this contract size bound. Each message is capped after redaction at 512 Unicode code points: an overlong value becomes its first 511 code points plus `…`.
- The outcome holds at most eight diagnostic entries. Eight or fewer remain unchanged. On overflow, retain the first seven; entry eight is exactly `stage=diagnostic`, `category=truncated`, `message=dropped=N`, with other optional keys absent. Worked example: nine inputs serialize entry eight as `{"category":"truncated","message":"dropped=2","stage":"diagnostic"}` because inputs eight plus nine were omitted.
- The budget permits at most three physical invocations, at most 15,000 ms cumulative sleep. An authoritative provider delay is a lower bound, never shortened. If the next required delay cannot fit, return `retry_not_before` without sleeping or incrementing invocation/request totals.
- After an ambiguous write, observe the desired primary-store postcondition before replay. Observed desired state produces `recovered`. Conclusive old state may replay if budget remains. Failed or inconclusive observation produces non-replaying `commit_unknown` with `ReplaySafety.forbidden`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/operation_outcome.py` — immutable provider-neutral values, bounded diagnostics, canonical serialization via the existing store seam.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/retry_budget.py` — sole three-invocation, 15-second fake-clock budget.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_operation_retry_budget.py` — deterministic contract, bounds, schedule, deadline, ambiguity tables.
- `docs/adr/0103-reconciler-operation-coordination.md` — provisional ownership/recovery decision.
- `docs/adr/README.md` — ADR index entry.

Grounding: `docs/adr/0084-acli-429-rate-limit-backoff.md` plus `acli_subprocess.py::_rate_limit_backoff` establish the existing additive-jitter formula. `docs/adr/0041-llm-diagnostic-sanitization.md` plus `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` establish allowlist-first redaction. Inspection shows that sanitizer does not enforce the ADR size promise, so this operation contract adds only its own size bound. `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` is the existing single canonical-JSON seam already used by reconciler modules.

## Testing
Use injected UUID, jitter, fake clock values. Table tests cover every enum member, canonical byte serialization, Unicode truncation, diagnostic overflow, all budget boundaries, provider delays that fit or exceed the remaining sleep budget, every ambiguity branch. Poison sleepers plus invocation counters prove rejected delays or `commit_unknown` perform no hidden work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The outcome field types expose exactly the enum member sets listed above; verified by exhaustive enum contract tests.
- [ ] Equivalent outcome values serialize through `canonical_bytes` to byte-identical compact UTF-8 JSON; verified by byte fixtures containing non-ASCII text.
- [ ] Diagnostic construction drops every field outside the six-key allowlist; verified with headers, bodies, credentials, ticket content.
- [ ] Diagnostic messages use the centralized redaction seam before persistence; verified with every ADR 0041 credential/PII pattern.
- [ ] Diagnostic truncation matches the 512-code-point rule plus the exact nine-input sentinel example; verified by Unicode boundary tables.
- [ ] One canonical logical id remains stable across three physical invocations; verified by an injected-UUID sequence.
- [ ] Invocation/request totals include only executed work; verified by counters on success, rejection, ambiguity paths.
- [ ] No schedule permits a fourth physical invocation; verified by an exhaustion table.
- [ ] No schedule permits cumulative sleep above 15,000 ms; verified at exact plus one-millisecond-over boundaries.
- [ ] Zero-based retry indexes produce `[2s,3s)` then `[4s,5s)` with no third sleep; verified at deterministic jitter endpoints.
- [ ] A fitting authoritative provider delay remains the sleep lower bound; verified with fake-clock tables.
- [ ] An over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without hidden work; verified by poison sleeper/counter assertions.
- [ ] Observed desired state returns `recovered`; verified by the desired-state ambiguity case.
- [ ] Conclusive old state replays only within remaining budget; verified by within-budget/exhausted tables.
- [ ] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`; verified by failure/inconclusive tables.
- [ ] Time-dependent tests complete with zero wall-clock sleep; verified by the injected fake clock.
- [ ] ADR 0103 records retry ownership, Jira non-idempotency, observe-before-replay, lifecycle owners, selected-route-only deltas, rollback, the ADR 0087 retry-ownership delta, desired-state deltas from ADRs 0004, 0026, and 0029, retained ADR 0084 additive jitter, and rejection of full/decorrelated jitter for only two bounded sleeps; verified by ADR numbering/index tests plus document inspection.

## Out of scope
Cloud/DC adapter execution, legacy dispatch integration, fuse consumption, production cutover are later tasks.
